title: Gate state names the run that produced it
description:
Pin with tests that an issue's gate state names the latest run recorded for that gate, so the pointer every latest-run reader relies on cannot regress.

## Background

`GateState.run_id: Option<GateRunId>` (`crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs`) is optional and skipped when absent. `gate_state_from_run` (`commands/gate_check.rs`) sets it for gate evaluation and lifecycle prechecks. A manual status write mints an attestation run and names it (the gate family's manual status write), and a newly required gate starts with none. No status write exists without a run. No test covers two evaluations in a row or names the attestation run on a manual write.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A unit test proves that evaluating a gate twice leaves `run_id` naming the second run.
- [hard] REQ-02: A unit test proves that a manual gate status write leaves `run_id` naming the attestation run that write recorded.

planning.outcome: Tests pin that a gate state names the latest run recorded for that gate.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two unit tests over a field and producers that exist.

title: Gate captures hold only the evaluated issue's latest runs
description:
Make gate evaluation, precheck planning and validation's precheck-history capture request only the runs the evaluated issue's gate states name, so the mutation image never holds another issue's runs.

## Background

A checker that consumes run history (`checker_consumes_run_history`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs`) receives the latest run of its gate on the evaluated issue (`compact_run_history_for_context`, `commands/gate_check.rs`). To find it, three captures list the whole `gate-runs/` root through `discover_gate_run_results` and take every run record into the image, then parse each one and keep those whose `issue_id` matches:

- gate evaluation: `capture_gate_evaluation_image`, parsed by `captured_gate_runs` (`commands/gate_check.rs`);
- precheck planning: `captured_precheck_plan` (`commands/mod.rs`);
- validation's precheck-history capture (`commands/validate.rs`).

The checker's issue view uses those runs too: `IssueShowResponse::from_issue` (`gate_check.rs`) builds every other gate's `last_run_at` and `exit_code` from them (`test_projected_precheck_run_matches_next_checker_issue_view`), so a capture restricted to history-consuming gates would null those fields. The precheck loop also appends each fresh result to the captured runs before the next gate.

`discover_gate_run_results` has a fourth caller that stays: `capture_record_fidelity_validation` (`commands/validate.rs`), which reads every run on whole-repository validation. `captured_gate_run_ids` (`repository_state/mutation.rs`) keeps that caller and `validation/record_fidelity.rs`.

The issue record's gate state names the latest run of each gate (`GateState.run_id`), so each record path is known from the issue record alone (`VirtualPath::gate_run_record`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: When any gate a capture serves consumes run history, the capture requests the run record that each required gate's state names on the evaluated issue, and nothing else under `gate-runs/`. None of the three captures lists the `gate-runs/` root.
- [hard] REQ-02: `capture_record_fidelity_validation` is the only caller of `discover_gate_run_results`, and `captured_gate_runs` reads no listing.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test shows that evaluating a history-consuming gate on one issue captures no run record of another issue, with other issues' runs present, and that the checker still receives the evaluated issue's latest run of that gate. `test_lifecycle_precheck_captures_large_history_and_ignores_root_clutter` no longer exists.
- [hard] REQ-04: `compact_run_history_for_context` selects by gate among the runs it receives: a gate with no named run passes the checker an empty history, a gate with one receives that run sanitized, and in the precheck loop the fresh result of a gate replaces its named run.

planning.outcome: Gate captures request the evaluated issue's named runs by path and list no gate-run root.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Three capture sites switch to one per-gate path request.

title: Gate-run records load by issue and run id
description:
Address a single gate-run record by its issue and its run id, so loading one run never needs to know where other issues' runs live.

`IssueStore::load_gate_run_result` (`crates/jit/src/storage/mod.rs`) takes a run id alone, implemented in `storage/json.rs` and `storage/memory.rs`; the test-only callers are in `storage/gate_runs.rs`, and two integration-test wrappers forward it (`tests/fast_docs_templates/template_apply_atomicity_tests.rs`, `tests/fast_rules/local_rule_enforcement_tests.rs`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `IssueStore::load_gate_run_result` takes `(&IssueId, &GateRunId)`. A record whose `issue_id` differs from the requested issue is reported as not found.
- [hard] REQ-02: The executor's `get_gate_run_result` takes the issue and the run id, the server's single-run route passes its issue path segment, and `projected_gate_run` passes its issue.
- [hard] REQ-03: One case in `storage/issue_store_conformance.rs`, run against both backends, proves that loading a run under the wrong issue is not found and loading it under its own issue returns it.
- [hard] REQ-04: A server test shows that requesting a run under another issue's path returns 404.

planning.outcome: One gate-run record loads by its issue id and run id through storage, the executor and the server route.

title: Latest-run readers use the gate-state accessor
description:
Make every reader of an issue's latest gate runs load one record per gate through one accessor, so showing an issue opens one run per gate instead of every run of the issue. Because this makes `GateState.run_id` the only route to a latest run, the same change moves the repository format to 4.

## Background

`get_last_gate_run` and `get_last_gate_runs_for_issue` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs`) already load the named run through `projected_gate_run` and list nothing. `IssueShowResponse::from_issue` still receives every run of the issue, from the issue family's show and status responses and from the show arm of `main.rs`, and `GateView::build` (`output.rs`) finds the named run in that list through `GateState::projected_run`.

`tests/cli_gate/gate_cli_integration_test.rs` (`test_issue_show_errors_on_corrupt_gate_run`) plants a corrupt run record that belongs to no issue and requires `issue show` to fail; a show that loads only named runs never opens it.

A redo record's puts follow the plan's action order (`redo_record_for`, `storage/repository_state_store.rs`). The finalizer (`repository_state/mutation.rs`) writes the issue record before the run record, and `load_issue` reads with no redo check. Once a show loads the run the issue names, a reader in the apply window, or after a crash until the next session completes the record, sees a run id with no record and fails with not-found.

`SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION` (`repository_state/index.rs`) is 3, and `docs/reference/storage-format.md` states that the marker changes whenever an on-disk interpretation changes. After this change a gate state without `run_id` has no latest run. Other repositories hold thousands of gate states with runs and no `run_id`, so a binary with this change must refuse them until they are rewritten. `tests/cli_repo_workflow/format_compat_cli_tests.rs` spells format 3 literally.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `get_last_gate_runs_for_issue` covers every gate state of the issue, one run per gate, loading each by `(issue, run)` and listing no runs. Unit tests show that it returns the named run when older runs of the gate exist, and nothing for a gate whose state has no `run_id` even when runs of it exist.
- [hard] REQ-02: The show, status, create and children responses take latest runs from that accessor, and none of them lists the issue's runs. `IssueShowResponse::from_issue` receives the latest run of each gate, and `GateView::build` selects nothing.
- [hard] REQ-03: History views (`gate status --all` and `--limit`, the server's run list) still list the issue's runs.
- [hard] REQ-04: `test_issue_show_errors_on_corrupt_gate_run` corrupts the run record that the shown issue's `run_id` names and `issue show` still fails on it.
- [hard] REQ-05: The finalizer orders a run record's write ahead of the issue record that names it, and a unit test pins that order in the composed redo record.
- [hard] REQ-06: `SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 4, a repository at format 3 is refused with the existing single-line error, and the format sample in `docs/reference/storage-format.md` shows 4. Tests derive the version from the constant, and the format-compatibility test's literal format is the supported one.

## Notes

- From this landing on, a build of main refuses this repository's own tracker, which stays at format 3 until the cutover window. The installed `jit` stays the last format 3 build, so gates, leads and workers are unaffected. Do not run `./scripts/install-jit.sh` from this commit onward until the window.

planning.outcome: Readers of an issue's latest gate runs load one record per gate through one accessor under repository format 4.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One existing lookup becomes the accessor, its remaining callers move onto it, and the format constant it forces changes with them.

title: Reused verdicts name their source issue and source run
description:
Make a reused gate verdict name the issue its source run belongs to as well as the run, in the stored record and in the web client's type, so the source record is addressable without searching.

## Background

`GateVerdictOrigin` (`crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs`) has three variants. `Reused(GateRunId)` names the source run by id alone and serializes adjacently tagged as `{"derivation": "reused", "source_run": "<run-id>"}`; `Executed` and `Attested` serialize as the tag alone, and a record without `origin` decodes as executed. Under per-issue run records the id alone does not locate the record.

Producer and readers: `reused_gate_run` (`commands/gate_check.rs`); the human render in `main.rs`; the generated storage-record reference (`storage/reference.rs` prose and sample), whose committed output `docs/reference/storage-records.md` is checked by `test_committed_reference_matches_projection`; the rustdoc of the provenance shape in `output.rs`. The web client's hand-written `GateVerdictOrigin` type (`web/src/types/models.ts`) declares `{ derivation: 'reused'; source_run: string }`; no web code reads `source_run` beyond the type.

Stored reused records in the old shape are rewritten by the format cutover. A repository at the old shape is refused by the format marker, which is already at 4 when this lands.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `GateVerdictOrigin` is internally tagged on `derivation`. `Reused` carries `source_issue: IssueId` and `source_run: GateRunId` and serializes as `{"derivation": "reused", "source_issue": "<issue-id>", "source_run": "<run-id>"}`; a record without `source_issue` fails to decode. `Executed` and `Attested` stay tag-only, and a record with no `origin` still decodes as executed.
- [hard] REQ-02: Reuse sets `source_issue` to the issue the source run belongs to, and the human gate-status render names both.
- [hard] REQ-03: The reference sample and prose and the `output.rs` rustdoc show the new shape, and the committed reference matches the projection.
- [hard] REQ-04: The web client's `GateVerdictOrigin` type carries `source_issue` beside `source_run`, and the web tests, lint and build pass.

planning.outcome: A reused verdict's provenance names its source issue and source run in the store, the server and the web type.

title: Recorded runs write their per-key verdict record
description:
Write, with each run that holds a reusable verdict, a record keyed by its gate and inputs digest that names the run, so reuse can later read one record.

## Background

Runs are written by the finalizer's gate-run pass (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs`). `GateRunResult::is_reusable_for` (`domain/types.rs`) states what makes a run a reuse source: it executed its own checker, carries an inputs digest and passed or failed. Only `check_gate_with` sets a digest. Gate keys are lowercase-kebab and digests 64 lowercase hex, so both are safe path components. Everything under `gate-runs/` is already excluded from input digests (`RepositoryLayout::tracker_written_paths`, `repository_state/path.rs`). The evaluation's record attempt captures its image in a second session (`commands/gate_check.rs`), after the digest is known. Whole-repository validation's fidelity pass (`validation/record_fidelity.rs`) is the guard that stored records reproduce, and it covers issues, the index, gate runs and the event log.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: When a recorded run executed its checker, carries an inputs digest and passed or failed, the same redo record that writes the run writes `gate-runs/verdicts/<gate-key>/<inputs-digest>.json` naming the run's issue and run id, built by one `VirtualPath` constructor. A later such run over the same key replaces the record. The record type derives `JsonSchema`.
- [hard] REQ-02: The record attempt captures the verdict record's path together with `gate-runs/verdicts` and `gate-runs/verdicts/<gate-key>`, which decide its directory creates, so two evaluations racing to replace one record get a retryable conflict, not a lost write.
- [hard] REQ-03: Finalizer unit tests show which runs write or replace a verdict record and which write none.
- [hard] REQ-04: `record_drift` reports a verdict record that does not reproduce, and the run enumeration of the fidelity pass skips `verdicts/`.

planning.outcome: Each run holding a reusable verdict writes its per-key verdict record in the same redo record.

title: Lease operations run through the lease lock
description:
Add a lease lock handle that holds the claims lock and offers load, list and apply, move acquire, renew, heartbeat, force-evict and release onto it, and make `claim list` and `claim status` read unexpired leases without the lock, marking stale ones, so every change shares one sequence and no reader waits on a writer.

## Background

`ClaimCoordinator` repeats the lock, load, evict, append and write steps by hand in each operation (`crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs`: `acquire_claim_synchronized`, `heartbeat`, `renew_lease`, `force_evict_lease`, `get_active_leases`). Today's store is the index `claims.index.json` plus the log `claims.jsonl`, written through `write_index_atomic` and `append_claim_op`. `CoordinationOrderGuard::enter` refuses while a repository order guard is held (`storage/guard_order.rs`), and the claims lock is `locks/claims.lock`.

`renew_lease` evicts an expired lease in memory and then fails as not found or not owned without writing the index, so the eviction is dropped and logged again by the next reader. `acquire_claim_synchronized` writes the index right after evicting. `evict_expired_at` appends the eviction record before removing the lease from the in-memory index. The indefinite-lease limits count every lease.

The claims family's release-by-issue operation takes the claims lock twice and lists every lease: once through `get_active_leases` and once per lease through `force_evict_lease`.

`claim list` and `claim status` are classified read-only (`cli.rs`) yet take the exclusive claims lock through `get_active_leases`, which also persists evictions (`test_get_active_leases_persists_eviction_of_expired_lease_once`). Claims-first mutations hold that lock across their repository session, so a listing waits on them, against @/charter/D-22. Their `stale` field is whatever the index stored, and `main.rs` renders a STALE block with a heartbeat remedy from it.

`read_leases`, `Lease::is_expired`, `Lease::is_stale` and `Lease::is_active` exist in `storage/claim_coordinator.rs`.

title: Gate runs are addressed per issue, per gate and per inputs digest
description:
Gate-run records are stored and read by key, so reading one issue's runs, its latest run of a gate, or a reusable verdict never reads another key's records.

## Background

Gate runs are stored flat, and readers enumerate and parse them. This story stores runs per issue, makes each issue's gate state the route to its latest run of a gate, finds reusable verdicts through a per-key verdict record, captures only the evaluated issue's named runs into gate mutations, and moves recorded runs into that layout through the format cutover.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Reading one issue's latest runs or its run history opens only that issue's run records.
- [hard] REQ-02: Reuse reads one verdict record and the run it names.
- [hard] REQ-03: Gate evaluation, precheck planning and validation capture no other issue's run records.
- [hard] REQ-04: This repository's recorded runs, latest-run references and verdict records are in the per-key layout, and every cited run id resolves.

planning.outcome: Gate-run records are stored and read per issue, per gate and per inputs digest.

title: Leases are per-issue records under one lease sequence
description:
Each lease is one record changed by one lock-load-change-publish sequence, and claims decide their event from the issue record, so no lease or claim operation reads the claims log or the event log's records.

## Background

The claims control plane keeps every lease in one index that is a second authority beside a replayed log, repeats its lock and publish steps in each operation, and keeps test-only APIs. The claim command parses the whole event log to decide its event. This story stores one record per lease, runs every lease change through one held lease lock, reads listings without that lock, addresses every lease command by issue, and makes a claim's event follow the assignee.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Reading or changing one issue's lease reads only that issue's lease record, and no lease operation reads the claims log.
- [hard] REQ-02: An interrupted lease operation leaves the prior or the next lease, and nothing rebuilds lease state from the log.
- [hard] REQ-03: A claim appends its event exactly when the assignee changes and parses no event-log record.
- [hard] REQ-04: Checkouts' leases are carried into lease records, and the lease docs describe them.

planning.outcome: Leases are per-issue records under one held lease lock, and claims decide their event from the assignee.

title: Only history-reporting commands read history files
description:
The event log, the claims log and gate-run history are append-only records that only history-reporting commands read, with one event-log parser, per-target archive evidence and a search that skips history by default.

## Background

Ordinary commands read the event log whole in captures, validation, archive planning and search, and a second event-log parser lives in the file backend's archive reader. This story gives the log one parser and one torn-line rule, moves archive evidence to per-target records, limits mutations to the log's bounded end and enforces that limit in the capture layer, names whole-repository validation as a history reader with its own read path, excludes history from default search, documents the history files and their readers, moves every repository to format 4, and proves the boundary end to end.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Exactly one event-log parser exists, with one torn-line rule, and an unknown tag is an error naming its line.
- [hard] REQ-02: Archive preview and execute read a target's evidence record once and never read the event log.
- [hard] REQ-03: The capture layer and the redo record admit only the end-of-log probe and the positioned append.
- [hard] REQ-04: An end-to-end test proves ordinary commands succeed over unparseable history files, and the storage references name the history files and their readers.

planning.outcome: Only history-reporting commands read history files, and the boundary is enforced, documented and tested.
